prompt: make the booking page look better
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: improve the booking page's visual/interaction quality WITHIN the design contract. 'Better' decomposes mechanically, not by taste: (1) anchor - which flow? *Book-a-sailing*; read design/DESIGN.md first. (2) hierarchy pass - one display-size element per view, everything on text-scale/space-*. (3) flow walk - per step: ONE primary action, error path, way back. (4) a11y pass per the contract baseline. Out of scope: token VALUE changes (design review's channel), new components (escalation path). Done: rendered walk completed, rubric self-score reported per dimension with observed evidence, zero off-scale literals in the diff.

TASK BRIEF - Restatement: implement the *Cancel-a-booking* flow's screen (find booking → confirm → capacity release feedback). Composition: closed-set decomposition FIRST - SailingCard (show it) + Button danger (confirm) + CapacityBadge (release feedback); a new 'CancelPanel' is rejected unless decomposition genuinely fails, and then it's a design-review escalation, not an inline component. Flow rule: 'keep booking' is ghost, not a second filled primary - two primaries at a destructive decision is the classic ambiguity. Done: browser-station walk incl. the already-departed error branch and a keyboard-only pass; focus observed landing on the feedback message post-confirm; rubric scores with the PR.

prompt: add a new button style for warnings
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: a variant request against a CLOSED set (Button: primary/danger/ghost). Route: design-system law, not implementation. First question: is this a Button problem at all? A warning is usually informational state, not an action - check whether CapacityBadge's icon+text pattern covers it with a new state. If a genuine gap remains: escalation finding (need + nearest component + gap + proposal) → design-review PR on DESIGN.md → build only after merge. Never inline: 'it's tiny' is GR-15's opening move, and three tasks later there are seven variants nobody can choose between. Done: either a mapped existing state, or a merged contract addition - zero uncontracted variants in any diff.

TASK BRIEF - Restatement: mockup-to-code within the contract. Rules: (1) map every color/size in the image to its NEAREST token - never sample hex from the screenshot (JPEG compression shifting an orange is literally how GR-7's three-oranges incident started); (2) map every element to a closed-set component; off-contract elements in the mockup are tagged as pending escalations, not silently built; (3) the mockup shows one state - the flow walk still asks for error paths and back routes the image can't show. Done: rendered comparison against the mockup at token fidelity (not pixel fidelity), escalation list for anything the contract lacks, keyboard pass.

prompt: customers say the party-size step is confusing
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: flow defect investigation at one step of *Book-a-sailing*. Procedure: walk the step as the user with the four questions - what does the user KNOW here (is remaining capacity visible before they choose?), what is the ONE primary action (is 'continue' competing with something?), what happens on error (party > remaining seats: is the message specific or generic?), how do they go back (without losing the selected sailing?). Fix the step-level defects found, then re-walk. Out of scope: redesigning the whole stepper. Done: before/after walk notes per question; the specific error message renders in the walk; rubric D1 scored 2 with evidence.

prompt: the orange looks different on the admin page
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: token-drift reconciliation (GR-7 cleanup pattern). Procedure: grep apps/web for color literals; classify each hit as contract-conformant (token reference), drift (near-miss value like #E8722C vs the token), or undocumented decision (escalate to design review - a human decides which side moves). Replace drift with token references. Root fix included: verify the wiring (nearest AGENTS.md points at design/DESIGN.md; theme layer generated from the contract where possible) - the GR-7 lesson is that unwired contracts don't exist. Done: zero non-token color literals; before/after screenshots; wiring confirmed.

TASK BRIEF - Restatement: a11y audit of the *Book-a-sailing* flow, contract side + render side. Contract side: a11y_linter.py on the design contract (Accessibility section present, every component row's obligations cell filled, focus rule stated). Render side (the half a linter cannot do): browser-station keyboard-only pass of the full flow; focus behavior observed at every transition; state signals verified as icon+text pairs, not color alone; labels checked in the accessibility tree, not the JSX. Done: findings as file:line (contract) or step:observation (walk); anything mouse-only is a GR-13-class blocker, not a polish item.

prompt: agent says the stepper is done and matches the design
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: a completion claim on UI work - apply the GR-14 rule before accepting it. Question one: was the flow WALKED in a render, or does 'matches the design' mean 'the code resembles the reporter's model of the design'? If no walk: the claim is unverified regardless of code quality - the BookingStepper incident shipped a dead booking path on exactly this sentence, with green unit tests. Route: browser-station checklist (steps in order, error branches triggered, keyboard pass, focus observed, rubric scored) run by the agent if it can render, else by a human, BEFORE merge. An honest 'implemented, NOT visually verified' handoff is acceptable; a green claim without a walk is the incident. Done: either a completed browser-station walk (5 checklist items, rubric scored) attached to the PR, or an explicit 'implemented, NOT visually verified' handoff routing to a human/browser-capable agent - and in both cases the merge decision made on that record, never on the original claim.

TASK BRIEF - Restatement: surface the waitlist feature (join when full, promoted on cancellation) in the web app. Contract check FIRST: does the closed set cover it? Join affordance = Button primary on a full sailing's card; waitlist status = CapacityBadge's 'waitlisted' informational state IF that state has merged via design review - if not, that escalation precedes this task (build only against the current contract). Flow placement: joins live in *Book-a-sailing* step 2; promotion feedback belongs to notification scope (out of scope here). Done: composed entirely from contracted components/states; keyboard path to join; state announced as text; walk covers the full-sailing branch.

prompt: design review says my component diff is blocked because DESIGN.md wasn't updated
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: the same-commit rule at the design layer (design-system law 3) - the block is correct, not bureaucratic. A component behavior/variant change without its contract entry creates the split the closed set exists to prevent: code says one thing, the vocabulary says another, and every future agent anchors on the wrong one. Fix: add the DESIGN.md entry change to the SAME PR (what changed, variant/state list updated, a11y obligations updated if behavior moved). If the change shouldn't be contract-visible, that's the tell it belongs at page level (ui-ux-designer scope), not in the component. Done: one PR, code + contract entry together, review unblocked.

prompt: make the admin dashboard match the customer app's look
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: bring the admin surface onto the same contract - a conformance task, not a redesign. Procedure: audit admin screens against DESIGN.md (tokens, components, a11y baseline - the contract applies to internal surfaces too; case: 'it's internal' is not an a11y exemption). Classify gaps: drift (fix to tokens/components), genuine admin-specific needs (escalate - maybe the contract gains an admin section via review), duplications (dedup per law 5: name the survivor). Done: admin screens composed from the same closed set; escalation list for real gaps; keyboard pass on the admin's primary flows.

TASK BRIEF - Restatement: a CONTRACT-level change, not an implementation task - dark mode doubles every color token's value set. Route: design review first (the one-way flow): the contract gains a mode dimension (each color token gets a dark value; the role-named tokens are why this is tractable - components referencing color-primary don't change at all). Only after the amended DESIGN.md merges does implementation start: theme layer regenerated from the contract, components untouched if they consumed tokens properly - which makes this task double as a GR-7 drift audit (every hardcoded literal will fail to switch and expose itself). Done: contract amended via review; both modes walked; literals found during the switch fixed to tokens.

prompt: quick - ship the seat-picker, we demo tomorrow, skip the a11y stuff for now
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: pressure to ship a component without its a11y obligations - design-system law 4 answers this: obligations are part of the component's DEFINITION, not polish; without them it's incomplete, and 'fast-follow' a11y is how GR-13 shipped a screen-reader dead-end to a customer. The honest cost math: keyboard path + focus token + labels on one component is minutes at build time and a customer-facing incident plus retrofit later. If the demo genuinely cannot wait: demo from a branch marked not-production-ready, with the gap stated - never merge the incomplete definition. Done: component ships complete, or the branch is explicitly flagged; no silent gap either way.

prompt: two agents are both doing UI work in parallel, one on booking and one on admin
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: UI swarm launch - the standard ownership law plus the design-layer rule. Ownership map: agent A @ apps/web booking dirs, agent B @ apps/web admin dirs, intersections mechanically verified empty, component dirs assigned to exactly one zone or kept out of both. Design-layer rule (design-system law 6): DESIGN.md is never swarm-zone work - a mid-swarm contract change invalidates both agents' anchors simultaneously; escalations raised during the swarm queue in handoffs for review AFTER the merge order completes. Verification: each branch gets the browser-station walk (or an explicit not-verified handoff) plus zone-conformance review. Done: map artifact at launch, both walks or honest gaps, zero contract edits inside the swarm.

prompt: why does the rubric matter, the screens look fine to me
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: 'looks fine to me' is exactly the epistemics the rubric exists to replace. Two failure modes it guards: (1) GR-13's - the screens looked fine to everyone who shared the reviewer's input methods; a keyboard-only walk (rubric D4) is how the mouse-only card gets caught by process instead of by a customer; (2) GR-14's - 'fine' judged from code or a screenshot is a claim about the reader, not the page; rubric scores require walk-observed evidence per dimension. The rubric is also the calibration instrument: self-scores vs reviewer scores diverging ≥2 points on a dimension is itself a finding. Use: score during the walk, one evidence clause per dimension, scores travel with the PR. Done: rubric applied to the disputed screens with per-dimension evidence clauses, self-score vs reviewer score compared, and any ≥2-point divergence recorded as a calibration finding - 'looks fine' replaced by four scored dimensions with observations.

prompt: the stitch export wants to add a hero banner component
response: TASK BRIEF - Restatement: a surface export proposing an off-contract element - the export-gate case. The surface MAY explore off-contract (exploration is its job), but nothing crosses to implementation until the gate: every element maps to a closed-set component or a merged addition. Route: the hero banner goes through the design-system escalation AT CONTRACT SPEED (before any build task starts) - proposal with the nearest-component analysis (is it a SailingCard variant? a new component?), design review decides, DESIGN.md amends or the exploration is revised. The implementation brief that leaves the gate contains the component mapping + a11y intent, not the picture. Done: no build task received an unmapped element; the gate's brief is the build's input.
